traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 315 Campanulaceae and 316 Lobeliaceae, which APG joins as Campanulaceae: herbs, rarely shrubs or small trees, nearly always with milky sap; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple; no stipules; bellflowers regular, with a bell- or tube-shaped corolla of 3 to 10 lobes (the lobelias' 5-lobed, two-lipped and turned over: so regular and irregular are both stated as often); ovary inferior, rarely superior; fruit a capsule opening in various ways, or a berry. Five lobes as typical from the lobelias' 5 and the bellflowers' commonest number (inferred).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Campanulaceae with Sphenocleaceae: its irregular flowers have a two-lipped corolla, read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy bilabiate. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 445, 447, family Campanulaceae: inflorescence raceme or cyme, rarely borne on the leaf, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "raceme": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 445, 447, family Campanulaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite [dioecious], usually; read as {"dioecious": "rarely", "hermaphrodite": "usually"}.
